tagline: The original superyacht coast — Monaco, Cannes and St-Tropez — with a year-round HNW commute layer.
summary: The French Riviera is the historic heart of the superyacht world: Monaco (Port Hercule, the Monaco Yacht Show), Antibes (Port Vauban, Europe's largest yacht harbour), Cannes and St-Tropez form a near-continuous luxury-marine corridor. Short coastal distances (Nice↔Monaco ~8 nm, Nice↔Cannes ~17 nm, Nice↔St-Tropez ~45 nm) make it a premium Pioneer II commute-and-charter corridor, layered over a real coastal commuter pain (the Basse Corniche and A8 are heavily congested).

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the entire Riviera corridor — Monaco (~8 nm), Cannes (~17 nm), Antibes, Îles de Lérins, St-Tropez (~45 nm) — for both charter tenders and executive commute.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) links the Riviera to Corsica and the Ligurian coast (Portofino/Genoa).

competitive_landscape: A vast superyacht fleet, Riviera Lines coastal ferries and event-driven charter demand operate today — deep demand and partner access (Monaco YC, IGY, Camper & Nicholsons). Summer road gridlock is the commuter pain. No foiling incumbent.
seasonality: Year-round HNW base with sharp event peaks (Monaco GP May, Cannes May, Yacht Show Sep); commute layer is non-seasonal.
regulatory_note: French flag / EU (and the Principality of Monaco); Affaires Maritimes certification; Monaco is a distinct jurisdiction with its own port authority. Riviera ports (Nice, Antibes, Cannes) are municipally/CCI managed.

precedents.why_it_matters: A wealthy, congested coastal corridor where a premium water tier serves both commute and luxury — the Riviera mirrors it.
